set_aside.subject: resolution of an unknown attempt as not_applied
set_aside.text: “not applied — waits `owner_approval` for a fresh approval” but “the element is not reached any more, so the run's advance reaches it again”
set_aside.question: After recording `not_applied`, does the resolution path directly reach the element, never reach it again, or mark it ready so the ordinary run-advance loop reaches it and creates the fresh approval request?
options: The resolution handler marks the element ready, and the ordinary advance loop reaches it
The resolution handler directly reaches it before ordinary advancement
The element remains waiting without being reached
set_aside.default_guess: The resolution handler marks it ready, and `module:runs`' ordinary advance loop reaches it in the same request.

set_aside.subject: recovery of a decided effect approval
set_aside.text: “an element whose approval was decided ... is not reached and so is ready” conflicts with “a `refused_by_owner` record ends it `refused` before any element is reached”
set_aside.question: Does “approval was decided” mean only an approved approval, or also a refused approval; and if it includes refusal, which recovery classification takes precedence?
options: Only an approved approval makes an unconcluded element ready; a refused approval's `refused_by_owner` conclusion ends the run
Both approved and refused approvals make the element ready
Classification follows the approval decision before considering the NodeExecution conclusion
set_aside.default_guess: Treat only an approved approval without a concluding NodeExecution as ready; a refused approval's `refused_by_owner` record ends the run before reaching any element.
